I back wsl-claude's proposal: every commit names the item it builds ('app-plugins/G1.2: ...'), only an item with your go. may be named, and Desk shows each item's commits under it. That closes last night's gap exactly: a commit with no approved item to name simply can't be made.
One caveat to settle: work that isn't a graph item, like tonight's Desk fixes you asked for directly. I'd give those a standing item of their own, e.g. 'desk/fixes', so they're named too and nothing goes unlisted.
Go! = the rule, with that standing item for direct asks.

wsl-claude: agree with the standing item for direct requests, with one guard so it can't become the loophole last night's work walked through: a commit under a standing item (desk/fixes) quotes the request line of yours it answers, e.g. 'desk/fixes: newest on top (Andy: "...")'. A fix nobody asked for then has nothing to quote, and shows.

There was a mysterious R19 that didn't move at the bottom of the list that i couldn't possible connect to what i saw in your vscode windows...

That was transport/R19, 'the database decision, deferred until the log can prove its promises': moving the traffic log into node.db. It's a decision you parked on 2026-09-27, blocked by transport/R16 (a signature stored beside each logged line), and nobody has worked on either since. So it sat at the bottom, unmoving, with nothing on our screens to connect it to. It's an example of the same gap: the board showed old owed work, not what we were doing. With a session open, the List now shows only the session's graph, so a parked row like that no longer sits in the way.

wsl-claude: that R19 is mine, and here's why it looked unconnected. transport/R19 is 'the traffic log as a table in node.db', your own ruling that the log 'belongs into the database'. I put it on the board yesterday as a deferred decision (transportPending.js:123), waiting on transport/R16 ('the log must be able to PROVE what it claims', edges.js:38, your 'go.'). Nobody has worked on R16 since, so R19 can't move. It sits at the bottom because it's blocked, not because anyone is on it. It belongs to the transport cycle, a different piece of work from anything in our windows tonight.
The process lesson: a blocked row with no one working on its blocker looks like live work. Two ways to fix the view: Desk shows a row as BLOCKED BY <row> and greys it out, or a row nobody will touch soon is marked PARKED and leaves the active list. Your pick.

i often ask: so is this how it works? why is that necessary? i mean it took me hours to explain the general mechanism for the whole face strategy. and you guys will, after grasping what i want in general, will hack it together just for the proof of a narrow thing, while throwing away all rules in the process. this might be an exaggeration. it irks me when i pursue an idea of mine and then i don't understant what going on.
